202
Top Universities of the world
*641. DR. ABHISHEK MANU
SINGHVI:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
Times Higher Education Supplement
recently produced a list of world's top
universities and a solitary Indian University
'JNU' appears at 192nd place;
(b) if so, whether it is a fact that the
criteria for top ranking places greater
emphasis on research and why we cannot
upgrade our few selected universities say
10 to 15, having significant input of quality
research; and
(c) whether Government would earmark
extra funds for universities initially and then
gradually ensure their autonomy to raise
their own funds in the long run?
Effect of slow legal procedure on
checking terrorism
*642. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN:
Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn to a US  Report wherein it has
been stated that India's counter-terrorism
efforts were hampered by its outdated and
overburdened law enforcement and legal
systems terming the Indian court system
slow, laborious, prone to corruption
and terrorism trials can take years to
complete;
(b) if so, the number of cases involving
terrorist activities which are pending in the
coutrs, State-wise;
(c) the number of cases of corruption in
judiciary that have come to notice of
Government during the last three years,
State-wise; and
(d) the steps Government propose to
take to wipe out corruption in judiciary
and address the problem of inordinate
delays?

203
Conduct of elections in Uttar Pradesh
*643. DR. P.C. ALEXANDER: Will the
Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of Central Police
personnel deployed for election duties in
Uttar Pradesh during the recent elections
to the State Legislative Assembly;
(b) the similar details about the State
police personnel;
(c) the number of officers from other
States deputed for the recent elections in
Uttar Pradesh;
(d) the estimates of cost incurred by
the State and Central Governments for
conducting these elections; and
(e) whether in view of the high costs
and labour involved in conducting elections
separately for State Assemblies and the Lok
Sabha, Government would consider making
arrangements for such elections to be
conducted simultaneously in future?
Vacancies of Judges of High Courts
and Supreme Court
*644. PROF. P.J. KURIEN: Will the
Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be
pleased to state:
(a) the total number of vacancies of
judges in the High Courts and Supreme
Court in the country and since how long
they are vacant;
(b) the steps taken by Government to
fill these vacancies;
(c) whether Government will consider
extending the retiring age of High Court
and Supreme Court Judges in order to avoid
the increase in the existing vacancies; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Ban on asbestos mining
†*645. SHRI KRISHAN LAL
BALMIKI: Will the Minister of MINES
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Indian Bureau
of Mines has conducted a study regarding
ill effects on the health of labourers engaged
in mining of asbestos;
(b) if so, whether such a study has
revealed any suggestions and whether the
study group has suggested to remove the
ban imposed on mining of asbestos;
(c) whether Government propose to
implement it and whether the ban imposed
on new lease deeds of asbestos mining and
renewal thereof will be removed; and
(d) if so, by when?
Scheme(s) for upgradation of food
processing industries in Goa
*646. SHRI SHANT ARAM
LAXMAN NAIK: Will the Minister of
FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be
pleased to state:
(a) whether any scheme(s) for
technology upgradation for food processing
industry is/are in force in Goa;
(b) if so, essential features of the
scheme(s);
(c) the projects undertaken/
implemented under the scheme(s) in the
last five years in the State; and
(d) the financial assistance granted to
the State during the last five years, year-
wise?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

Danger of global warming
4897. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will
the Minister of EARTH SCIENCES be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Mumbai
finds a place in the list of areas that face the
danger of global warming;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether other coastal cities are also
included in the list, if so, the names thereof;
and
(d) the measures/steps being taken by
Government in this regard?
Upgradation of seismic residence in
Delhi
4898. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the
Minister of EARTH SCIENCES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
Delhi falls under Seismic Zone IV and it
has more than 1.5 lakh residential buildings
vulnerable to earthquake; and
(b) the action plan of Government to
guide the residents of Delhi to go in for
retrofitting to upgrade the seismic
resistance of their houses?
Tamil Nadu under seismic
zone
4899. SHRI K.P.K. KUMARAN: Will
the Minister of EARTH SCIENCES be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
the people of Tamil Nadu are very much
disturbed on the branding of parts of their
State as they are coming under Seismic
Zones No. 2 and No.3; and
(b) whether Government would issue
a confirmatory statement to the effect that
no area other than the three districts, which
have been selected for installing earthquake
measuring equipments, is earthquake
prone in the State; as farmers are being
threatened by a neighbouring State where
earthquake is being used as a weapon to
question the safety of a dam in the border
area?

1139
Expansion of Metallurgical extraction
facilities
4900. SHRI SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
Will the Minister of EARTH
SCIENCES be pleased to state:
(a) the details of the progress made in the
Poly Metallic Nodule Programme in terms of
mining of nodules during last five years;
(b) whether Government propose to
expand the metallurgical extraction facilities
and their capacity; and
(c) whether the programme has attained
commercial viability?
Food processing units in the country
†4901. SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY: Will the Minister of FOOD
PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) the total number of units of this
industry throughout the country and the
number of such companies in private and
public sector, separately;
(b) whether Government provide some
incentives to States and the State-wise
number of such units; and
(c) the employment generated from this
industry so far?
Plan for encouragement of food
processing industries in the country
†4902. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
Will the Minister of FOOD
PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have prepared a plan with the help of big
industrialists to prepare infrastructure to
encourage food processing industries in the
country;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the ratio
of participation of Government and private
sector in this plan; and
(c) by when, this plan will be
implemented in the country?
Fund for cold storage facilities in the
country
4903. DR. K. MALAISAMY: Will
the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) the total demand, allocation and
utilization of funds besides the subsidy
percentage under cold storage/warehouse
facilities in the country;
(b) whether while comparing the felt
need of this facility and the allotment made,
is it not a neglected area left out without
due consideration; and
(c) the perspective plan and the time
frame to fulfil this commitment?
Scheme for capacity of food
processing and cold storage facilities
†4904. SHRI AMIR ALAM KHAN:
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
formulated any scheme to enhance the
capacity of food processing and cold
storages in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
